entries.title: Leviticus 23:2
segments: Holy convocations; assemblies for religious purposes.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:3
segments: No other seasons or occasions of public worship are ever to set aside, supersede, or lead nay to neglect the habitual and holy observance of the weekly Sabbath.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:5
segments:
First month; Abib or Nisan, the first month of the ecclesiastical and the seventh of the civil year; answering to the last part of March and the first part of April. 
 
  The Lord's passover;

The reasons why believers in Christ are passed over or spared, and made partakers of the riches of grace, should ever be remembered, and the love which procured their salvation be celebrated according to his command, with gratitude and joy.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:10
segments: Shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits; this sheaf, as well as the accompanying offerings,
, was presented to the Lord by the priest in the name of the whole congregation.  It is thought to have been a sheaf of barley, which begun to be ready for the harvest at the passover.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:11
segments:
Wave the sheaf; as a sign of consecreation to the Lord. 
 
  On the morrow after the sabbath; the Jews understood the Sabbath here to mean not the weekly Sabbath, but the first day of unleavened bread, which was kept as a Sabbath,
.  As this fell on the fifteenth of the month Abib, the sheaf was presented on the sixteenth.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:14
segments:
Bread--parched corn--green ears; that is, of the new crop. 
 
The blessings of providence, as well as of grace, are from the Lord. They should all be acknolwedged as his gifts, and used to his glory.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:15
segments: From the morrow after the sabbath; see note to

. 
 
  Seven sabbaths; seven weeks or forty-nine days.  These with the preceding day, the first day of unleavened bread, made fifty days. Hence this was called the feast of Pentecost, a Greek word meaning, The fifieth.  It was a feast of thanksgiving at the close of the harvest, which began about the time of the passover.  It also coincided with the giving of the law on Sinai, and was afterwards made memorable by the gift of the Holy Spirit.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:16
segments: A new meat-offering; made of the new flour.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:17
segments: Bring out of your habitations; the people seem to have generally brought on this occasion, offerings of flour made from the new corn. From a portion of these, two loaves were made and offered by the priest, with the accompanying sacrifices and oblations,
, in the name of the whole congregation.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:21
segments: After gathering in the fruits of the earth, a day of annual thanksgiving, appropriately observed by all the people in commemoration of the goodness of God, is suited to honor him and benefit them.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:24
segments: The seventh month; Tishri.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:27
segments: Afflict your souls; by fasting and confession of sin.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:31
segments:
A statute; a law that the tenth day of Tishri should be observed as a sabbath, or day of atonement, of rest, and of religious worship.  It was a day of annual fasting, humiliation, and prayer. 
 
A day annually, of humiliation, fasting, and prayer, when labor and amusements are suspended, and the people unite in confessing and forsaking their sins and imploring divine mercy, is highly proper, and has often been blessed.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:34
segments: Feast of tabernacles; in commemoration of their having dwelt in tabernacles during forty years in the wilderness.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:40
segments: Deliverances from great evils, as well as the reception of great favors, call for peculiar gratitude to God, and should be celebrated with special thanksgiving.

entries.title: Leviticus 23:42
segments: Booths; temporary dwellings, made of boughs or other slight materials.
